title: Lumped capacitance cooling: when a hot part cools as one temperature
examples: What is the lumped capacitance method?
How long does a hot steel ball take to cool?

curves.label: Steel ball 10 mm
curves.ask: What does the lumped cooling curve look like?

explain.say: A blacksmith pulls a small steel ball bearing out of the furnace at 500 degrees and leaves it in a 25 degree breeze. How fast does it cool? For small metal parts there is a lovely shortcut: treat the whole part as one temperature. Look at the two cases on the board.

draw.text: Lumped capacitance cooling: when a hot part cools as one temperature

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Use the lumped method only when Bi < 0.1

draw.text: Steel ball, D = 10 mm, from 500 °C in air at 25 °C, h = 100

explain.say: The shortcut works when heat moves through the inside far more easily than it leaves the surface. The Biot number measures that: h times the volume over area, divided by k. For our ball, 100 times 1.67 millimetres over 45 gives 0.004. Under 0.1, so the inside stays almost even. What about a thick concrete block?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Use the lumped method only when Bi < 0.1

explain.say: Its Biot number is large, so its core stays hot while the skin cools: no shortcut. For the ball, an energy balance gives an exponential decay. The time constant, tau, is rho c V over h A: 7800 times 470 times 0.00167 over 100, about 61 seconds. See the curve fall?

curves.label: Steel ball 10 mm
curves.ask: What does the lumped cooling curve look like?

explain.say: After one time constant, the ball has lost 63 percent of its excess temperature: it is about 200 degrees. After two minutes, the temperature is 25 plus 475 times e to the minus 120 over 61, about 92 degrees. See the second mark? How would a fan, which doubles h, change tau?

curves.label: Steel ball 10 mm
curves.ask: What does the lumped cooling curve look like?

explain.say: It would halve tau, so it cools twice as fast! Wonderful. Real link: thermocouples are made tiny so their tau is short and they respond quickly. Exam tip: always check Bi below 0.1 first, and use V over A, which is D over 6 for a sphere.

curves.ask: What does the lumped cooling curve look like?

draw.text: Sphere: V/A = D/6; cylinder: V/A = D/4 (long)

faq.q: What is the lumped capacitance method?
faq.a: Treating a cooling or heating body as one uniform temperature, so its temperature decays exponentially towards the surroundings. It works when the Biot number is below 0.1.

faq.q: What does the lumped cooling curve look like?
faq.a: An exponential decay towards the surrounding temperature: T minus T infinity equals the initial difference times e to the minus t over tau.
asks: how long does a hot steel ball take to cool

faq.a: Bi equals h times the characteristic length, volume over surface area, divided by the conductivity of the solid. It compares resistance inside the body with resistance at its surface.

faq.q: What is the time constant in lumped cooling?
faq.a: Tau equals rho c V over h A. After one tau, 63 percent of the temperature difference has gone; after about five, the body has practically reached the surroundings.

faq.q: Why are thermocouples made very small?
faq.a: A small bead has little mass for its surface area, so its time constant is short and it follows temperature changes quickly.

facts: The lumped method is accurate to about 5 % when the Biot number is below 0.1.
After one time constant, an exponential cooling has completed 63 % of its change.

quiz.say: A part has a time constant of 50 seconds and starts 200 degrees above the air. Roughly how far above the air is it after 50 seconds?
quiz.show: τ = 50 s; starts 200 K above the air. Excess temperature after 50 s?

wrong.1: That is how much it has dropped, 63 %, not what is left.
wrong.2: Exponential decay is not a straight halving in one time constant.

quiz.say: When is the lumped capacitance method valid?
quiz.show: The lumped capacitance method is valid when…

options.show: The Biot number is below about 0.1
options.say: The Biot number is below about 0.1

options.show: The body is larger than 1 metre
options.say: The body is larger than 1 metre

quiz.why: A small Biot number means the inside conducts heat far more easily than the surface loses it.

wrong.1: Large bodies usually have large Biot numbers, the opposite.
wrong.2: The Reynolds number describes the flow, not the temperature inside the body.
